---
title: "Hiring CV Bias"
subtitle: "Errors of a CV parser and their effect on the selection of candidates"
toc: false
---

::: {.authors}
Francesco Baiocchi and Leonardo Petrilli · University of Bologna
:::

::: {.abstract}
Recruiting agencies use a *parser* to turn a CV into a structured profile, and a *matcher* to rank the profiles
against the job offers. On anonymized data from Adecco we study both steps in two projects. The first, for *AI in
Industry*, measures what the parser misses in the CVs and whether its errors differ across groups. The second, for
*Ethics in Artificial Intelligence*, follows those errors down to the selection: do they change who is selected for a
job, and do they penalize some groups more than others?
:::

## The pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  CV["CV text"] -- parser --> P["Structured profile<br/>licenses, languages, job titles, skills"]
  P -- matcher --> S["Score of every<br/>(candidate, job) pair"]
  S --> L["Position in<br/>the job's list"]
```

An error of the parser is information that is written in the CV but missing from the profile. The first project
measures these errors; the second follows them down to the position of the candidate in each job's list.

## The two projects

### Bias of the CV parser (*AI in Industry*)

We compare what the proprietary parser extracts with what is written in the CV text, using our own extractors:
regular expressions for driving licenses and languages, exact and semantic matching against the ESCO occupations for
job titles. We then test whether the parser's errors differ across gender, macro-region and CV length.

- [Problem statement](pages/01-problem.qmd): the questions we ask of the parser.
- [Pipeline](pages/02-pipeline.qmd): cleaning, exploration, distributions and bias detection.
- [Results](pages/03-results.qmd): the errors of the parser and the bias metrics per group.

### Fairness audit of the selection (*Ethics in Artificial Intelligence*, Module 2)

We reconstruct Adecco's matcher from its outputs, score every (candidate, job) pair with the parser's profile and with
the corrected one, and compare the two selections with the three criteria of group fairness: independence,
separation and sufficiency.

- [Fairness audit](pages/04-fairness-audit.qmd): the four phases and their results.
- [Slides](pages/05-presentation.qmd): the presentation of the audit.
- Notebooks: [data audit and protocol](notebooks/ethics/data_audit_and_protocol.ipynb),
  [propagation](notebooks/ethics/propagation.ipynb), [mitigation](notebooks/ethics/mitigation.ipynb).

## Main results

- The parser misses much of what is written in the CVs: its recall against our extractors is 0.41 for driving
  licenses, 0.66 for languages and 0.55 for job titles. Across groups no strong bias emerges.
- Adecco's score is a weighted sum of seven components: our formula reproduces 99.88% of the scores without outliers
  exactly.
- Correcting the parser's errors changes 8.3% of the selections. Every group is selected at the same rate
  (independence holds), but the decisions on southern candidates are wrong more often (separation and sufficiency
  fail), mostly because southern job lists cannot separate their candidates.
- The mitigation techniques of the course have little to act on in the real system; a toy case shows them where they
  can be applied.

## Repository

```text
hiring_cv_bias/
├── bias_detection/              # AI in Industry: errors of the parser
├── cleaning/                    # cleaning of the raw CVs
├── exploration/                 # distributions and disparity metrics
├── hard_soft_skills_labelling/  # hard and soft skills
├── translation/                 # CVs into English
├── reverse_matching/            # AI Ethics, phase 1: the pairs dataset
└── fairness/                    # AI Ethics, phases 2 to 4

notebooks/
├── ai_in_industry/              # cleaning, exploration, distributions, bias
└── ethics/                      # audit and protocol, propagation, mitigation

tests/                           # unit tests
```

The CV data are anonymized but proprietary, so they are not in the repository. The unit tests and the toy mitigation
example run without them. The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/francescobaio/hiring_cv_bias).
